summary: No entropy floor on any signing key or credential (runtimecfg)
description:
**Surfaced by TKT-245's ai-review [high], confirmed, and NOT specific to that ticket.**

`runtimecfg.RequiredCredential` (`shared/go/runtimecfg/runtimecfg.go:123-158`) validates **transport
characters** — emptiness, retired literals, edge whitespace, header-safety — and never **entropy or
length**. A deployment configured with `x` starts cleanly.

This guards **every credential in the system**, so the exposure is system-wide rather than catalog's:

| Value | Service | Consequence of a weak value |
|---|---|---|
| `COMMERCE_CUSTOMER_ASSERTION_KEY` | commerce | forge a customer assertion → attribute orders to any buyer |
| `CATALOG_ORGANIZER_ASSERTION_KEY` | catalog | forge an organizer assertion → write into any tenant (TKT-245/ADR-058) |
| `ACCESS_TICKET_LINK_KEY`, `ACCESS_QR_PRIVATE_KEY` | access | forge ticket links / QR payloads |
| `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`, the three staff-write tokens, `PAYMENTS_INTERNAL_TOKEN` | all | bearer credentials, brute-forceable online |

The **signing keys** are the sharper half: a captured token gives an offline oracle, so a weak key
falls without touching the service at all.

**Conditions of Success:**
- A `runtimecfg.RequiredSigningKey` (or an entropy floor on `RequiredCredential`) that requires a
  minimum of 32 random bytes, in a declared encoding, and refuses anything shorter.
- Adopted by **both** assertion keys at once, and by the ticket-link/QR keys. Adopting it in one
  service is the failure mode this ticket exists to avoid: it would leave the identical hole one
  service over while looking closed.
- Startup tests proving short and malformed keys are refused, and that the error **never echoes the
  value** (the existing credential tests already assert this and are the pattern to copy).
- A decision recorded on whether existing deployments need a rotation, since a value that starts
  today may not start after this lands — that is a deploy-ordering question, not just a code one.

Quality gates: `make check`. Touches `shared/go`, so every service rebuilds.

Non-goals: rotation mechanics or key overlap (no service has them today; ADR-058 § consequences
records that for catalog).

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Filed from TKT-245's ai-review — confirmed, and deliberately NOT fixed there

ai-review raised this as **[high] "Catalog accepts trivially brute-forceable HMAC signing keys"**.
Correct, and verified: `RequiredCredential` has no length or entropy check.

**Why it was overridden rather than fixed in TKT-245.** The same function guards every credential in
the system, including `COMMERCE_CUSTOMER_ASSERTION_KEY` — the **direct precedent** for TKT-245's
mechanism, with an identical threat model, shipped in TKT-221 with the same absence. So TKT-245
*inherits* a system-wide property rather than introducing one.

A catalog-only entropy floor would have been worse than none: it would leave the identical hole one
service over while **looking** like the class had been addressed — the "configured-looking and wrong"
failure ADR-042's own credential guard exists to prevent. The fix belongs in the shared package, used
by both assertion keys at once.

**What already holds, and what does not:** `make up` and `scripts/env-bootstrap.sh` generate 32 bytes
from `/dev/urandom`, compose ships no default and refuses to start without the variable, and no
signing key is ever sent to a web process. None of that is *enforcement* — it is a convention a
production deployment can decline to follow, which is exactly the reviewer's point.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Shaping pass — 7 of 8 DoR items met, `approach` held OPEN for a human decision

Ticket claim **verified against the code**: `RequiredCredential` (`shared/go/runtimecfg/runtimecfg.go:123-159`)
checks emptiness, the retired literal, edge whitespace and `httpguts.ValidHeaderFieldValue`, and
nothing else. `x` starts cleanly. 14 credential loads across 6 binaries inherit that.

**The ticket's proposed remedy does not survive the read**, and the corrections are worth more to
the planner than the original wording:

1. **The floor cannot be uniform.** Three encodings coexist. The two Ed25519 seeds
   (`ACCESS_QR_PRIVATE_KEY`, `ACCESS_LIFECYCLE_PRIVATE_KEY`) already decode
   `base64.RawStdEncoding` and refuse anything but exactly `ed25519.SeedSize` — `token.go:37-39`,
   `keys.go:61-67`. They need **no floor**, only a test pinning that they are covered. So the COS
   clause *"adopted by the ticket-link/QR keys"* is half already-true and half genuinely open:
   `ACCESS_TICKET_LINK_KEY` is a **raw-string HMAC key with no floor at all** (`server.go:65`).
2. **`JOURNAL_SIGNING_KEY`'s 16-byte floor is not an oversight.** `ADR-032` line 115 enumerates
   *"a secret under 16 bytes"* as a blessed rejected configuration, and `docs/development.md:448`
   rests the key-id log-safety argument on the explicit sentence *"nothing here requires
   `JOURNAL_SIGNING_KEY` to be high-entropy."* Raising 16→32 is an **ADR amendment plus a docs
   correction**, not a code change — and `main_test.go:145` asserts on the literal substring `"16"`.
3. **A length floor is not an entropy floor.** Thirty-two `a`s passes any `len()` check. The honest
   claim is a *length* floor that makes online brute force infeasible for values the generators
   already produce; the word "entropy" should not reach the error message or the ADR.
4. **`ADR-056` lines 61-72 is the in-repo precedent for the number** — *"a generated 32-byte
   token… 256 bits"*. Cite it rather than inventing 32.

**Ordering hazard, pinned as a governing test.** `runtimecfg.go:130-136` carries an explicit
`ORDER MATTERS` comment. A length case placed anywhere but **last** rewrites the message for the 9
sub-cases of `TestRequiredCredentialRejectsValuesHTTPWouldChange` and breaks two **exact-string**
assertions (`runtimecfg_test.go:109`, `:120`). Note the retired literal `local-service-token` is 19
chars — it must still reach the *retired-default* case, not the new length case.

**Guaranteed fixture breakage, and it is the bulk of the work.**
`TestAcceptedCredentialSurvivesAnHTTPRoundTripUnchanged` (`:199`) is a **positive** test with
fixtures of 9, 6 and 10 chars — lengthen them, do not delete the case, it exists to prove interior
spaces survive an HTTP round trip. And `scripts/smoke.sh:196-197,209` carries 30/31-byte journal
literals **co-owned** with `journal_smoke_test.go:45-49` under the `TestSmokeJournalKeyLiteralsMatchScript`
drift guard (TKT-117) — edit both or neither. Full radius in the mémo (~10 lines of production code
against 12+ test files and 2 shell scripts).

**No generated value breaks.** `env-bootstrap.sh` and `stack-env.sh` draw 32 bytes from
`/dev/urandom` (64 hex chars) and `compose.yaml` ships `${VAR:?}` with no defaults. That is the
argument for a hard refusal over a deprecation window — but it is Q3's to settle, not shaping's.

**A gap the COS asks for that does not exist yet:** there is **no** test asserting the error omits
the value on `RequiredCredential` *itself*. The no-echo assertions live on the `InternalTokenFromEnv`
wrapper and on caller guards. COS clause 3 is new work, not a copy of an existing pattern.

---

### ⛔ Gate 1 is HELD — `approach: open`, `owner: human`

Per `shaping.md`, `approach: deferred` **does not pass** when a ticket touches auth, and this one is
the auth substrate for every credential in the system. Three questions, one answer each:

- **Q1 — What does the floor measure?** Raw byte length of the configured string (simple, testable,
  satisfied by every generator at 64 chars) **or** decoded material per declared encoding
  (correct-sounding, but teaches `runtimecfg` three encodings and buys nothing for the two seeds
  that already enforce exactly 32)?
- **Q2 — Does `JOURNAL_SIGNING_KEY` go 16→32 in this ticket** (carrying the ADR-032 amendment, the
  `development.md:448` correction and the `main_test.go:145` expectation), **or stay at 16** with the
  divergence recorded as deliberate?
- **Q3 — Do existing deployments need a rotation?** Hard refusal at startup (a value that boots today
  stops booting) or a deprecation window? The ticket's own COS asks for this to be decided.

`risk:low` **not claimed** — auth surface, shared package, all six binaries rebuild, >5 files.

**8 governing ADRs baked into the context-mémo, every one verified to resolve at HEAD**
(`ADR-012/021/032/042/043/056/057/058`), plus 6 governing tests. Next ADR number: **ADR-059**.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 — the three open decisions are answered by the owner; `approach` flips to `met`

**Q1 — What does the floor measure? → RAW BYTE LENGTH of the configured string.**
`len(token)`, not decoded material per declared encoding. The decoded version sounds more correct
and is the trap: `runtimecfg` currently knows nothing about any encoding *deliberately* — it
validates transport characters, which is encoding-agnostic — so teaching it three encodings means 14
new per-caller declarations and a new way to be wrong. It also buys nothing: the two credentials
where decoding matters already refuse anything but exactly `ed25519.SeedSize` **at their own decode
sites** (`token.go:37-39`, `keys.go:61-67`), which is the tier their mechanism actually lives at.
The nine raw-string credentials have no encoding to decode — their string *is* the key material.

ADR-059 must say **length floor**, not entropy floor. It defeats online brute force; it certifies
nothing about entropy, and the error message must not claim otherwise.

**Q2 — `JOURNAL_SIGNING_KEY` 16→32? → NO. It stays at 16, and the divergence is recorded.**
ADR-032 line 115 is a *decision*, not an accident, and the journal key is **absent from this
ticket's own threat table** — its exposure is different in kind: it signs an append-only audit
journal verified offline by an operator, not a credential an attacker presents. Raising it would
pull in an ADR-032 amendment, the `development.md:448` correction, the `main_test.go:145`
expectation and both smoke literals with their drift guard — all as a side effect of a different
ticket, which is exactly the move the plan gate exists to catch. If 16 is wrong it earns its own
ticket. **ADR-059 states plainly why the two numbers differ**: a recorded divergence is a decision,
an unrecorded one is drift.

**Q3 — Rotation for existing deployments? → NO WINDOW. Hard refusal at startup.**
No generator produces a short value: `env-bootstrap.sh` and `stack-env.sh` draw 32 bytes from
`/dev/urandom` (64 hex chars), `access keygen` emits 43-char base64, `compose.yaml` ships
`${VAR:?}` with no defaults. Any deployment on the documented path already passes, so a window
would protect only a hand-written short key — precisely what this ticket exists to stop, and a
warning that lets it keep booting is the "configured-looking and wrong" failure ADR-042's guard
exists to prevent.

**The cost is real and goes in the ADR rather than being assumed away:** an operator who *did*
hand-write a short key discovers it at **restart**, not at deploy time. That is the right trade —
the fix is `openssl rand -hex 32`, the alternative is leaving a forgeable signing key live — but it
is written down.

---

### Resulting shape (the planner's starting point, not the plan)

- `minCredentialLen = 32`, appended **LAST** in the `RequiredCredential` switch — the `ORDER MATTERS`
  comment at `runtimecfg.go:130-136` and the two exact-string assertions are why.
- **One refusal test per credential, at its own call site.** Not one test on the shared helper: a
  green test one tier above the mechanism proves the fake and the handler agree and nothing else
  (AGENTS.md).
- The **missing** direct no-echo assertion on `RequiredCredential` itself — today it exists only on
  the `InternalTokenFromEnv` wrapper and on caller guards, so COS clause 3 is new work.
- Lengthened fixtures across ~12 test files, plus `scripts/smoke.sh:196-197,209` **and**
  `journal_smoke_test.go:45-49` together under their drift guard.
- **ADR-059** — the floor, the 16-vs-32 divergence and its reason, the no-window call and its
  operational cost.

**DoR: 8/8 met. No open blockers.** `risk:low` **not claimed** — auth surface, shared package, all
six binaries rebuild, >5 files. Gate 1 cleared by the owner → **Ready**.

objective.note: runtimecfg.RequiredCredential validates transport characters only (empty, retired literal, edge whitespace, httpguts) and never length or entropy. Verified at shared/go/runtimecfg/runtimecfg.go:123-159. A deployment configured with `x` starts cleanly across 14 credential loads in 6 binaries.

scope.note: IN: an entropy floor in shared/go/runtimecfg, adopted at once by the 9 raw-string credentials (INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN, PAYMENTS_INTERNAL_TOKEN, the 3 staff-write tokens, both assertion keys, ACCESS_TICKET_LINK_KEY) + a decision recorded for the 2 Ed25519 seeds and JOURNAL_SIGNING_KEY; an ADR (ADR-059) stating the floor and the rotation position; fixture/literal migration everywhere the floor now bites. OUT: rotation mechanics, key overlap, mTLS, per-caller credentials, web/backoffice credentials.mjs beyond a stated decision.

uncertainties.note: Resolved by reading rather than by spike. (1) THE FLOOR CANNOT BE UNIFORM: three encodings coexist - raw string (9 vars), base64 RawStdEncoding->ed25519.SeedSize (ACCESS_QR_PRIVATE_KEY token.go:33-39, ACCESS_LIFECYCLE_PRIVATE_KEY keys.go:61-67, both ALREADY exactly 32 decoded bytes and already enforced), and raw bytes with an existing 16-byte floor (JOURNAL_SIGNING_KEY, keyring.go:16 minSecretLen). A single '32 bytes in a declared encoding' rule as the ticket text words it would either double-count the base64 seeds (43 chars pass a 32-char test trivially and prove nothing new) or contradict a shipped ADR. (2) A string-length floor is NOT an entropy floor: 32 repetitions of 'a' passes any len() check. The honest claim is a LENGTH floor that makes online brute force infeasible for values the generators already produce at 64 hex chars; say that, do not write 'entropy' into the error or the ADR. (3) Ordering hazard: the length case must go LAST in the switch - runtimecfg.go:130-136 carries an explicit ORDER MATTERS comment and 9 sub-cases of TestRequiredCredentialRejectsValuesHTTPWouldChange plus 2 exact-string assertions (runtimecfg_test.go:109, :120) expect the existing messages.

dependencies.note: No open blockers, no blocked-by links. Touches shared/go so all 5 services + gateway rebuild. Two co-owned literal sets must move together or a drift guard fails: scripts/smoke.sh:196-197,209 and services/payments/internal/store/journal_smoke_test.go:45-49, pinned by TestSmokeJournalKeyLiteralsMatchScript (journal_smoke_test.go:701, TKT-117).

approach.note: RESOLVED by the owner at Gate 1 (three decisions, recorded in the kind=readiness comment below). A1: the floor measures RAW BYTE LENGTH of the configured string - len(token) - not decoded material per encoding; runtimecfg stays encoding-agnostic and the two Ed25519 seeds keep enforcing exactly 32 decoded bytes at their own decode sites, which is the tier their mechanism lives at. A2: JOURNAL_SIGNING_KEY STAYS AT 16; ADR-032 line 115 is a shipped decision, the journal key is absent from this ticket's own threat table, and overriding it as a side effect of another ticket is out of scope - ADR-059 records WHY the two numbers differ. A3: HARD REFUSAL at startup, no deprecation window, because no generator produces a short value (env-bootstrap.sh/stack-env.sh draw 32 bytes from /dev/urandom, compose ships ${VAR:?} with no defaults) so a window would protect only the hand-written short key this ticket exists to stop; the operational cost - an operator with a hand-written short key discovers it at restart - is recorded in ADR-059 rather than assumed away. SHAPE: a minCredentialLen=32 case appended LAST in the RequiredCredential switch; one refusal test per credential AT ITS OWN CALL SITE (not one test on the shared helper); the missing direct no-echo assertion on RequiredCredential itself; lengthened fixtures across ~12 test files + scripts/smoke.sh literals with their drift guard; ADR-059.

first_slice.note: One slice, and it must be one: the ticket exists precisely because a per-service adoption 'would leave the identical hole one service over while looking closed'. Slice = the floor in shared/go/runtimecfg + adoption by all 9 raw-string credentials + ACCESS_TICKET_LINK_KEY + the ADR + fixture migration. Sized by the fixture blast radius, not the logic: ~10 lines of production code against 12+ test files and 2 shell scripts.

success.note: COS restated with the read applied: (1) a length floor in runtimecfg refusing values below the declared minimum, placed AFTER the existing cases so every current message survives; (2) adopted by both assertion keys AND ACCESS_TICKET_LINK_KEY in the same change, with a test per credential proving the refusal - not one test for the shared helper (a green test one tier above the mechanism proves the fake and the handler agree, AGENTS.md); (3) the error never echoes the value, asserted directly on RequiredCredential, which today has NO such test - the no-echo assertions live only on the InternalTokenFromEnv wrapper and on caller guards; (4) the rotation/deploy-ordering decision recorded in ADR-059; (5) make check green, including the smoke journal literals and their drift guard.

context_memo.note: Baked below; 8 governing ADRs all verified to resolve at HEAD.

governingAdrs.constrains: Line 115 BLESSES the 16-byte journal floor as a stated rejected-configuration list. Raising JOURNAL_SIGNING_KEY to 32 CONTRADICTS a shipped ADR and requires an amendment here, not a silent bump. Also explains (line ~118+) why HMAC key comparison is on the EFFECTIVE key: RFC 2104 zero-pads short keys and digests long ones, so byte-distinct values can be the same HMAC key - directly relevant to any reasoning about what a short key costs.

The in-repo precedent for the NUMBER: line 61 'SHA-256 over a generated 32-byte token', line 72 'this token is 256 bits' and bcrypt's cost 'exists to compensate for low-entropy human-chosen secrets'. Cite this for the floor's value rather than inventing 32.

Defines CATALOG_ORGANIZER_ASSERTION_KEY (HMAC-SHA256, line 63) and states the consequence this ticket bounds - line 189 'anyone holding the signing key mints for any organizer, forever'. States NO minimum length; ADR-059 should say so explicitly rather than implying it always did.

The staff-write credential separation (and the TKT-194 amendment at line 290 adding the money-moving one). Establishes 'generated independently' as the standard but states no length requirement - the gap ADR-059 closes.

NAME THE ADVERSARY before writing any strength claim. Also D4 (line 240-243): lifecycle Ed25519 material is deliberately namespaced apart from QR. Both seeds are already length-correct; the ADR is why they must stay distinct.
ACCESS_QR_PRIVATE_KEY is injected configuration; its seed decode already pins ed25519.SeedSize.
Where an auth guard belongs - the floor goes in the shared package the 14 loads already call, not in each caller.
INVENTORY_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN, the third staff-write credential; line 156 enumerates the four credential classes this floor must cover at once.

governingTests.why: 9 sub-cases whose fixtures are 6-24 chars and which assert on the WHITESPACE and HEADER-VALUE messages. A length check placed before them rewrites the message and fails all 9. The floor case must be LAST.

EXACT-STRING equality on the error text. Any reworded message, including appending a length clause, fails these two. The retired literal 'local-service-token' is 19 chars, so it must still reach the retired-default case, not the new length case.

A POSITIVE test whose 4 fixtures include 'a-b_c.d~e' (9), 'tok en' (6), 'Zm9vYmFy==' (10). GUARANTEED breakage under any floor. It exists to prove interior spaces survive an HTTP round trip - lengthen the fixtures, do not delete the case.

Reads scripts/smoke.sh and fails if the literal sets drift (TKT-117). smoke.sh:196-197,209 carry 30- and 31-byte journal keys; journal_smoke_test.go:45-49 owns the same four literals. Edit both or neither.

A table case asserting on the literal substring '16' for the short-secret rejection. If Q2 raises the journal floor, this expectation moves; if Q2 leaves it at 16, it must stay untouched - which is itself the evidence that the divergence was deliberate.

governingTests.test: shared/go/runtimecfg/runtimecfg_test.go has NO length test and NO direct no-echo test on RequiredCredential
governingTests.why: The no-echo assertions are on the InternalTokenFromEnv wrapper (:109, :120) and on caller guards (catalog/credentials_test.go:36,87; commerce:48; payments/main_test.go:162,183-190). COS clause 3 asks for the assertion on RequiredCredential itself - it does not exist yet, so it is new work, not a copy.

callSites.note: 14 credential loads across 6 binaries - a per-service fix is the failure mode this ticket exists to avoid.

fixtureBlastRadius: scripts/smoke.sh:196,197,209 (30/31-byte journal literals, co-owned with the drift guard)
services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go:1596,1601; channels_test.go:47 (19-28 chars, construct servers directly - unaffected by a runtimecfg floor, affected by a setter floor)

web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts:50,54,56,316,329,343,356,649,683 (14-25 chars) and web/backoffice/credentials.mjs:36-59 assertCredentialSeparation - presence + pairwise distinctness only, NO length check. The third place a system-wide floor would have to land.
context.generatorsAlreadySafe: scripts/env-bootstrap.sh:72-76,97 and scripts/stack-env.sh:47-125 all draw `od -An -tx1 -N32 /dev/urandom` = 64 hex chars; access keygen emits 43-char base64 seeds. compose.yaml ships ${VAR:?} with no defaults. So no GENERATED value breaks under a 32-byte floor - only hand-written fixtures and the smoke literals do. This is what makes the floor cheap to adopt and is the argument for a hard refusal over a deprecation window (Q3).
docsToCorrect: docs/development.md:448 - 'nothing here requires JOURNAL_SIGNING_KEY to be high-entropy' underpins the key-id log-safety argument; if Q2 raises the journal floor this paragraph is stale.
docs/adr/ADR-032 line 115 - the blessed 'under 16 bytes' rejection.
context.nextAdrNumber: ADR-059 (ADR-058 is the highest at HEAD)
